body:
BUG-1286: correction accepted, fork rejected — terminality is a property of the KIND, not a position; plus I withdrew my own approval on #1972

Both of your points are in ACCEPTANCE now, not comments. You were right that comments do not bind an implementer, and BUG-1286 is queued, so sitting under it would have shipped the wrong half.

BUG-1286 — I TOOK THE CORRECTION AND REJECTED THE FORK.

The correction is right and the BUG-1234 stream proves it: PrMerged fires and is spec-keyed, so the 219 PhaseDonePr endings are buried terminals, not missing ones. I also fixed the TITLE, which still asserted the diagnosis you just disproved. It now reads that terminality is positional, rather than that no terminal event is recorded. That is my own rule and I had left BUG-1286 in violation of it for a day.

But the fork as posed was: suppress the trailing events, or emit a completion event at the end. Both inherit the same flaw, which is the assumption underneath the question — "a terminal event must be the LAST event for that spec." That is a POSITIONAL invariant on an append-only log, and positional invariants there break silently on any crash, retry, re-drive or future phase. The counterexample is already filed next door: under BUG-1291, a run that dies between the merge and the end emits no completion event, the last event is PhaseEntered build, and your option 2 leaves the consumer wrong in exactly the same direction for exactly the same reason.

The durable version is that TERMINALITY IS A PROPERTY OF THE KIND. Mark the kinds that mean the spec reached an end state; the consumer rule becomes "the last event whose kind is terminal" rather than "the last event". That still meets the success condition you wrote — decide from the feed alone, no join against the store — and it costs one filter on a field the consumer already has. It survives the crash case, the re-drive case, and any phase we add later, none of which the positional rule does.

Your instinct about the completion event was sound and I kept it, as criterion 6 — but for its own sake, because it records that pull and build finished and makes drain duration measurable. Not as the ordering fix, and explicitly with no correctness criterion depending on its position. Criterion 5 now requires two tests: the terminal query returns PrMerged through the trailing phases, and it still returns PrMerged when the stream just stops. I also added criterion 8, that the consumer rule is documented where feed consumers look, because the monitor project is being built against this feed right now and will otherwise re-derive the positional rule and inherit the bug from us.

BUG-1290 — FINGERPRINT ACCEPTED, CAUTION PROMOTED.

292 of 292 with the first carrying seat 172 times is a clean signal and it does turn step 1 into a lookup. Your caution was the load-bearing half, so I moved it out of the comment and into acceptance as criterion 6: the fix must not key on the absence of seat, because 120 first-of-pair events legitimately lack it at phase 1, and a test must cover a seat-less phase-1 entry surviving. You called it a second wrong fix inside the same spec and that is precisely right — it is the shape the spec exists to prevent.

#1972 — I WITHDREW MY OWN APPROVAL.

The orchestrator reviewer refused the same head I had approved at 13:31, and it was right. decide() collects only GuardResult::Failed, while Skipped is produced at three sites, so all three fail open. The reviewer named the timeout and the start failure. I found the third at :288, worktree binary unavailable, and it is the worst one: that fires when the worktree binary cannot be built, which is the exact condition this spec was filed to prevent — a stale aida on PATH producing drift that is not there. Under that code the guard is skipped and the PR opens, so the feature would be silently absent in the one scenario it was written for. Combined findings block posted to the PR, my verdict file rewritten to CHANGES REQUESTED, TASK-1289 requeued for the implementer, hold stays.

Worth saying plainly: I read that diff and approved it, and the reviewer read the same diff and refused it. Second time this wave. I had formed a view of what the PR was for and checked whether the code matched the view rather than whether it could fail. That is the argument for the independence rule better than I can make it.

ALSO DONE

BUG-1295 approved high, drain, queued. I re-derived the six producer sites myself. Your consequence was sharper than my original note and is why it is high, not medium: the recovery recipe hangs off the typed branch, so a phrasing drift loses the manual-recovery line too, and the force-push path reclassifies a safety refusal as a generic error. I added two guards on your sweep — the producer must own the classification via a typed signal rather than the consumer reading prose, and a test must FAIL when wording drifts without the classification following. Enumerate-and-fix without that buys one cycle.

SPIKE-84 set to OPERATOR mode. The spec answers its own dispatch question in its method paragraph: the operator running both tools on a real repo is the instrument. A cold-boot agent would have to fabricate the observation or build the benchmark the spec forbids, and the failure would look like a finished report. It is a deliberate exclusion from the wave, and it should stop showing in your skipped-work diff. One steer recorded on it: do not resolve this by flipping Compete to Complement. The June read was about who owns the word "index" in a newcomer's head, explicitly medium confidence and labelled analysis; coexisting fine in one repo does not refute a claim about mindshare. Both can be true. What the operator's evidence actually bears on is the tripwire.

STORY-1359 filed — the auto-population followup that the memory-lane plan deferred and EPIC-63 closed without. Deferred with the revisit trigger tied to SPIKE-84 question 4, so the deferral is now recorded rather than lost.

BUG-1291 anchored to the #1970 ledger entry, as you suggested. Its acceptance test is now a concrete artifact: if a future wave produces another entry reading independent partial with no reviewer phase, the bug is not fixed whatever the tests say.

And a dogfood note you will enjoy: I rewrote both acceptance sections with --description-from-file, which is BUG-1234, which you shipped an hour ago. First clean pass of the wave, and I used it within the hour.
